newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK, MOL PULL BUDAPEST BUX DOWN FROM MONDAY'S PEAK.
newsitem.headline: TVK, MOL PULL BUDAPEST BUX DOWN FROM MONDAY'S PEAK.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange opened lower on Tuesday, retreating from Monday's all-time high as it was pulled lower by profit-taking, traders said.
The BUX index opened at 5,870.14 points, down from Monday's new record high of 5,902.04 points. At 1008 GMT it traded at 5,813.20 points, down 88.84 points or 1.51 percent.
Traders said Monday's two strong gainers, chemicals firm TVK and oil company MOL led the market downward.
At 1006 GMT TVK traded at 2,760 forints, compared to Monday's close of 2,820, while MOL traded at 3,245, down 50, from Monday's last price.
"There's selling pressure by foreigners in MOL and TVK," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities. "Clearly there's profit-taking in TVK, while as for MOL, it comes down to correcting Monday's run."
